stem:
The diagram shows Gopal completing a mirror image across a fixed horizontal symmetry line. Point $B$ is $4\,\mathrm{cm}$ above the line, at a marked horizontal position.

Where does the reflected point $B'$ belong?

options.text: $B'$ is $4\,\mathrm{cm}$ below the line, at the same horizontal position as $B$.
$B'$ is the name mirror image for the symmetry line itself.
$B'$ may sit anywhere below the line, at any distance.
First place $B'$, and that placement is what creates the symmetry line.

teacher.key_rationale: Reflection across a horizontal line sends a point 4 cm above to 4 cm below at the same horizontal position. Treating B' as a name for the line swaps terms. Any distance below omits equal distance. Saying B' creates the line reverses the relation.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right triangle as a horizontal mirror line with B and B'.
